title: Skin biopsy
what: Using local numbing, the doctor takes a small piece of skin, or the whole growth, and sends it to be checked under a microscope.
why: When it is not clear from looking what a spot, mole, or rash is.
tell_doctor: Allergy to numbing medicine, iodine, or tape
If you tend to get thick scars

prepare.title: Preparation
prepare.text: No special preparation is needed. You can usually eat as normal.

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: On the day of the procedure, do not put cream or makeup on that spot.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop blood thinners on your own. Tell your doctor and they will decide.

steps: The doctor looks at the spot and cleans the skin
You get a numbing injection and the skin goes numb
With a small tool, the doctor takes a piece of skin
The wound is closed with a stitch or tape, or sealed with heat
The piece goes into a small jar and is sent to the lab
feel: The numbing shot stings for a few seconds
After that, only pressure. It should not hurt
When the numbing wears off, the wound may ache a little
after: Usually keep the bandage dry for 1 to 2 days
Care for the wound the way your doctor told you
Stitches usually come out after 7 to 14 days, depending on the spot
red_flags: Bleeding that does not stop after pressing the wound for 15 to 20 minutes
Growing redness, swelling, and pain, pus, or a fever

faq.q: Is it dangerous to biopsy a mole?
faq.a: No. A biopsy does not make a mole more dangerous. It is needed to find out exactly what it is.
Usually a small one that fades over time. Ask your doctor ahead of time where it will be and what it will look like.
